extracted.intended_audience: interested persons and potential parties in the FERC docket (landowners, community organizations, Tribal members, businesses, ratepayers, and other members of the public)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural guidance for submitting comments, protests, and motions to intervene in a FERC section 7(c)/Part 157 docket (CP25-533-000), including filing methods, deadlines, service rules, and environmental-review timing. Useful for members of the public and organizations seeking to participate or obtain party status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ways to participate in the Commission's review
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three ways to become involved in the Commission's review of this project: you can file comments on the project, you can protest the filing, and you can file a motion to intervene in the proceeding. There is no fee or cost for filing comments or intervening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the appropriate method based on whether you only wish to express support/concern (comments), formally oppose (protest), or become a party with litigation rights (motion to intervene). The deadline for filing a motion to intervene is specified below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person wishing to comment on the project may do so. Comments may include statements of support or objections, to the project as a whole or specific aspects of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The more specific your comments, the more useful they will be. Comments do not make the filer a party to the proceeding. To be timely and properly recorded, reference the docket number (CP25-533-000) and submit by the stated deadline. Methods: eComment (brief text-only), eFiling (attach files), or mail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protests
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to sections 157.10(a)(4) and 385.211 of the Commission's regulations under the NGA, any person may file a protest to the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protests must comply with the requirements specified in section 385.2001 of the Commission's regulations. A protest may also serve as a motion to intervene so long as the protestor states it also seeks to be an intervenor. Reference docket CP25-533-000 and file by the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to intervene — eligibility and required content
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person (including individuals, organizations, businesses, municipalities, and other entities) has the option to file a motion to intervene in this proceeding. Only intervenors have the right to request rehearing of Commission orders and to subsequently challenge the Commission's orders in the U.S. Circuit Courts of Appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A motion to intervene must be submitted in accordance with Rule 214 of the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure and the regulations under the NGA. Your motion must state, to the extent known, your position regarding the proceeding and your interest in the proceeding (for an individual: landowner, ratepayer, resident of an impacted community, or recreationist). You do not need to have property directly impacted to intervene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention deadline and timeliness rules
rubrics_metrics.description: To intervene, you must submit a motion to intervene by the intervention deadline for the project, which is 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on September 12, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All timely, unopposed motions to intervene are automatically granted by operation of Rule 214(c)(1). Motions to intervene filed after the intervention deadline are untimely and may be denied. Any late-filed motion must show good cause for being late and explain why the time limitation should be waived, providing justification by reference to the factors set forth in Rule 214(d). The applicant has 15 days from the submittal of a motion to intervene to file a written objection to the intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to file comments or protests (methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three methods you can use to submit your comments or protests to the Commission. In all instances, please reference the Project docket number CP25-533-000 in your submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1) eComment feature on www.ferc.gov for brief text-only comments. 2) eFiling on www.ferc.gov under Documents and Filings — allows attachments; new eFiling users must create an account via eRegister and select 'General' then 'Comment on a Filing'. 3) Paper copy by mail or courier to specified addresses (USPS or other courier addresses provided). The Commission encourages electronic filing and provides eFiling staff assistance (contact numbers/emails).

rubrics_metrics.name: How to file a motion to intervene (methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two ways to submit your motion to intervene. In both instances, please reference the Project docket number CP25-533-000 in your submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1) eFiling feature (www.ferc.gov) — new users must eRegister; select 'General' then 'Intervention'. The eFiling feature includes a document-less intervention option (link provided). 2) File a paper copy of your motion to intervene, along with three copies, by mail/courier to the specified addresses. The Commission encourages electronic filing and offers eFiling support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service requirements for protests and motions to intervene
rubrics_metrics.description: Protests and motions to intervene must be served on the applicant either by mail at the applicant's postal address or by email (with a link to the document).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any subsequent submissions by an intervenor must be served on the applicant and all other parties to the proceeding. Contact information for parties can be downloaded from the service list at the eService link on FERC Online. Service can be via email with a link to the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference docket number in all submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: In all instances, please reference the Project docket number CP25-533-000 in your submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including the docket number ensures your comments/protest/intervention are timely and properly recorded. Omission may lead to misfiling or failure to associate your submission with the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental review timing and notice (section 157.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to section 157.9 of the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure, within 90 days of this Notice the Commission staff will either: complete its environmental review and place it into the Commission's public record (eLibrary) for this proceeding; or issue a Notice of Schedule for Environmental Review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a Notice of Schedule is issued, it will indicate milestones and the anticipated date for issuance of the final environmental impact statement (FEIS) or environmental assessment (EA). The filing of an EA or issuance of a Notice of Schedule notifies federal and state agencies of the timing and the need to complete all federal authorizations within 90 days of the date of issuance of the Commission staff's FEIS or EA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement on environmental mailing list
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons who comment on the environmental review of this project will be placed on the Commission's environmental mailing list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those on the mailing list will receive notification when the environmental documents (EA or EIS) are issued for this project and will be notified of meetings associated with the Commission's environmental review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Party status and service list benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: A person obtaining party status will be placed on the service list maintained by the Secretary of the Commission and will receive copies (paper or electronic) of all documents filed by the applicant and by all other parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being on the service list ensures receipt of formal documents, filings, and updates throughout the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public assistance resources and contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission's Office of Public Participation (OPP) supports meaningful public engagement and can help members of the public access information and navigate Commission processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For public inquiries and assistance with filings such as interventions, comments, or requests for rehearing, contact OPP at (202) 502-6595 or OPP@ferc.gov. eFiling staff assistance is available at (202) 502-8258 or FercOnlineSupport@ferc.gov. The Public Reference Room contact information is also provided for assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: eSubscription for tracking proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission offers eSubscription which allows you to keep track of formal issuances and submittals in specific dockets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eSubscription provides notifications, document summaries, and direct links to documents, reducing the time spent researching proceedings and keeping you informed of filings and issuances in the docket.
